corrected_content.problem:
Consider the curves $C_{1}$ and $C_{2}$, defined parametrically as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:\hspace{1em}{\mathbf{r}}_{1}(t) & =⟨\operatorname{sin}t,\hspace{0.222em}\operatorname{cos}t⟩, & 0\le t\le 2\pi  \\ {C}_{2}:\hspace{1em}{\mathbf{r}}_{2}(\theta ) & =⟨\operatorname{sin}2\theta ,\hspace{0.222em}\operatorname{cos}2\theta ⟩, & 0\le \theta \le \pi \end{aligned}
$$

Now suppose $$
\displaystyle \int_{C_{1}}f(x, y)ds = k
$$ for some function $f(x, y)$ and real number $k$. Which of the following must be true?

1. $$
\displaystyle \int_{-C_{1}}f(x, y)ds = k
$$
2. $$
\displaystyle \int_{C_{2}}f(x, y)ds = k
$$
3. $$
\displaystyle \int_{C_{2}}f(x, y)ds = \frac{1}{2}k
$$
corrected_content.worked_solution: Scalar line integrals are independent of orientation, so I holds. Set $t=2\theta$; as $\theta$ runs from $0$ to $\pi$, $t$ runs from $0$ to $2\pi$. Both parametrizations therefore traverse the same circle once, giving the same integral $k$. Thus II holds. III does not hold for arbitrary $k$, so the statements that must be true are I and II.
